title: Closed universal isomorphism locus for a finite-free quotient on a flat integral-fibre family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-affine-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Assume every fibre is nonempty and geometrically integral: after every extension of its residue field it is a nonempty reduced irreducible scheme [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Let $n\geq0$, let $G$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], and let $u:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow G$ be a surjective module-sheaf morphism. Then there is a closed immersion $i:Z\to S$ of finite presentation [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that, for every scheme $T$ and every $h:T\to S$, $h$ factors through $i$ if and only if the tensor pullback $u_T:\mathcal O_{X_T}^{\oplus n}\to G_T$ is an isomorphism, where $X_T=X\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $G_T$ and $u_T$ are pulled back along $X_T\to X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. This factorization is unique whenever it exists.

source.place: Tag 05PF (theorem-flattening-map), with source module O_X^{oplus n}; Tag 05K5 (lemma-flat-geometrically-integral-fibres-pure) supplies universal purity of O_X. Finite direct sums have the same associated-point support for n>0; n=0 is the zero module.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$. By [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $X_V=f^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine. The affine criteria [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] make $A\to B$ flat and finitely presented. For $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a field extension $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the corresponding extended fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A L)$. It is nonempty and integral by the hypothesis. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], its affine coordinate ring $B\otimes_A L$ is a nonzero domain. Thus the affine algebra has precisely the geometrically integral fibres required below.

source.place: Tag 05FT (lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian), hypotheses; affine translation by Schemes Tag 01I4 and Morphisms Tag 01TQ

proof.text: Set $M=B^{\oplus n}$ and $N=\Gamma(X_V,G|_{X_V})$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], $N$ is finitely presented over $B$. The affine equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $u|_{X_V}$ with a $B$-linear map $v:M\to N$. This map is surjective: the image computation on affine opens in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identifies $\operatorname{im}(v)$ with the global sections of the image sheaf, which equals $G|_{X_V}$ because $u$ is surjective. Write $K=\ker v$. For any $A$-algebra $C$, the pullback of $u$ to $X_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}C$ is identified with $v_C=v\otimes_A1_C$. Indeed the ring of that affine scheme is $B\otimes_A C$, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], and the naturality formula of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives the map $v\otimes_B1_{B\otimes_A C}$; the identification with $v_C$ sends $m\otimes(b\otimes c)$ to $bm\otimes c$, with inverse $m\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Pullbacks are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], so the affine equivalence detects whether this map is an isomorphism.

Apply [lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective] to $A\to B$, using step 1: $B$ is projective as an $A$-module. By the split-free characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose $A$-linear maps $j_0:B\to F_0$ and $r_0:F_0\to B$, where $F_0=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}A$, with $r_0j_0=1$. Taking $n$ copies gives $j:M\to F=F_0^{\oplus n}$ and $r:F\to M$ with $rj=1$. The vectors indexed by $\{1,\ldots,n\}\times\Lambda$ form a basis of $F$, directly by the definition of a direct sum. No finiteness of $\Lambda$ is required; when $n=0$, $M=F=0$.

Let $I\subseteq A$ be the ideal generated by every basis coefficient of every vector $j(k)$ with $k\in K$. For an $A$-algebra $C$ with structure map $\varphi:A\to C$, [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $K\to M\to N\to0$ says that $v_C$ is surjective and its kernel is the image of $K\otimes_A C$. Tensoring $rj=1$ keeps $j_C$ split injective. Thus $v_C$ is an isomorphism exactly when $j(k)\otimes1=0$ for every $k\in K$. To check that condition, the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identifies $F\otimes_A C$ with the free $C$-module on the same basis, sending $e_\lambda\otimes c$ to $ce_\lambda$; its inverse sends each basis vector to $e_\lambda\otimes1$. The coefficients of $j(k)\otimes1$ are therefore the images under $\varphi$ of those of $j(k)$. Vanishing of all these coefficients is equivalent to $\varphi(I)=0$. This proves $v_C$ invertible if and only if $I\subseteq\ker\varphi$, for every $C$, including nonreduced rings and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 05PE (lemma-flattening-module-map), explicit coefficient-ideal argument, expanded using Algebra Tag 00DF

proof.text: The ideal $I$ is finitely generated. Since $M$ is finite free over $B$ and $N$ is finitely presented over $B$, [lem-trf-finite-presentation-surjective-module-kernel] gives $B$-generators $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ of $K$. Step 4 with $C=A/I$ shows that all $k_i$ map to zero in $M\otimes_A A/I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] applied to $I\to A\to A/I\to0$, the kernel of $M\to M\otimes_A A/I$ consists exactly of finite sums $\sum a_\ell m_\ell$ with $a_\ell\in I$ and $m_\ell\in M$. Choose such an expression for each of the finitely many $k_i$, and let $J\subseteq I$ be generated by the finitely many coefficients occurring in these expressions. Then $k_i\in JM$. Because $JM$ is a $B$-submodule of $M$ ($b(am)=a(bm)$), it contains all of $K$. Right exactness now gives that $v_{A/J}$ is an isomorphism. Step 4 forces $I\subseteq J$, so $I=J$ is finitely generated. This argument does not assume that $B$, $M$ or $N$ is finite over $A$.

source.place: Tag 05PE (lemma-flattening-module-map), with finite-presentation refinement; algebra.tex Tag 0519 (lemma-extension), part (5), and Tag 00DF

proof.text: Put $Z_V=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ over $V$. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] this is a closed immersion. Its ideal sheaf is $\widetilde I$ by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; the finite list of generators of $I$ gives a finite-type sheaf by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Hence [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] makes $Z_V\to V$ finitely presented. On an affine $V$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$, the spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the quotient-ring universal property give a unique factorization through $Z_V$ exactly when $I$ maps to zero in $C$. Steps 2 and 4 identify this with invertibility of $u_C$. For an arbitrary $V$-scheme $T$, cover $T$ by affine opens. The inverse maps of a sheaf isomorphism agree on overlaps by uniqueness of inverse, so invertibility of $u_T$ is equivalent to invertibility on these opens. The local factorizations through $Z_V$ also agree: on an affine refinement of any overlap they are the unique ring maps from $A/I$ extending the given map from $A$, and thus glue as scheme morphisms. Consequently $Z_V$ has the required universal property on every $T$, with unique factorization.

source.place: Tag 01TV (lemma-closed-immersion-finite-presentation); schemes.tex Tags 01QO and 01JC for affine quotients and gluing

proof.text: Define $P(T,h)$ to mean that $u_T$ is an isomorphism. Restricting to an open of $T$ restricts the same module map, by the composition law in [def-pc-module-pullback]. Thus $P$ restricts to opens. If it holds on a neighbourhood of every point of $T$, those neighbourhoods pull back to a cover of $X_T$, and their inverse module maps agree on overlaps; gluing them gives the inverse of $u_T$. Apply [lem-sc-local-closed-locus-gluing] with this predicate and the closed finitely presented schemes $Z_V\to V$ constructed in step 6 for affine opens covering $S$. It gives a closed immersion $i:Z\to S$, locally of finite presentation, with the stated factorization equivalence on all schemes. On each $V$, its restriction is $Z_V$: the two universal properties give inverse maps, since factorization through an affine quotient is unique as established in step 6. Its ideal sheaf therefore restricts to $\widetilde I$, a finite-type module, on every $V$. Finite type is local by [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], so [lem-trf-closed-immersion-finite-presentation-ideal] makes $i$ of finite presentation. Any two factorizations of $h:T\to S$ agree on an affine refinement of the preimages of the $V$, by the uniqueness in step 6, hence agree globally. For $n=0$, surjectivity gives $G=0$, the construction has $K=I=0$ on every chart, and $Z=S$, as required.
